summary: Tested Blog Autopilot end-to-end (backend API + admin UI) plus regressions. 49 backend assertions across 6 pytest files: 47 passed, 2 failed and both are the SAME data defect (one legacy AI post left in DB with a dirty slug containing ':' and a curly apostrophe). New autopilot generation is correct: real Gemini call (~1-2 min budget, actual ~90s and ~35s runs), clean [a-z0-9-] slug, 8-12 body paragraphs, title/excerpt/category/tags, ai_generated=true, published and publicly fetchable at GET /api/blog/<slug> (200). GET/PUT settings persist (incl. clamping 0->1, 5000->90, partial updates don't clear other fields) and require admin JWT (401 without). Admin UI verified: Blog & insights panel -> Blog Autopilot box, enable toggle + frequency persist across reload with 'Autopilot updated' toast, 'Generate a post now' shows 'Writing…' disabled state then success toast with post title, post count 25 -> 26, status row updates (generated_count 3->4, last run, next scheduled). Public homepage and generated post page render cleanly (no webpack overlay, 12 paragraphs, cover image). Regressions passed: lead delete, seo.google_verification save, marketing.popup_enabled persistence, case studies CRUD.

minor.issue: Legacy AI post still has a dirty slug: 'why-you-need-a-freelance-ai-consultant-in-2026:-a-leader’s-guide' (colon + U+2019). It was created before the _slug() fix, so the fix is correct but old data was not migrated — the public URL is ugly/encoded and would be a bad canonical/sitemap entry. Recommend a one-time re-slug migration (or delete that post).

Response returns _get_autopilot() only — omits next_topic and next_run (unlike GET). The admin status row therefore blanks out 'Next topic'/'Next scheduled' immediately after saving until reload (reproduced in UI screenshot). Return the same enriched payload as GET.

Uses re.sub(r'[^\w\s-]', ..., flags=re.UNICODE), so non-ASCII word chars (accents, Devanagari) survive into slugs. Consider unicodedata NFKD + ASCII fold, and add an explicit slug re-check/regex guard before insert in generate_blog_post().

integration_issues.issue: After a successful save the status row loses 'Next topic' and 'Next scheduled' values (backend PUT response lacks those keys); values return after page reload

issues: React hydration error: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' logged on /admin — some select renders an element inside <option>
Invalid DOM property warning: fetchpriority should be fetchPriority (BlogPost.jsx:72, ServiceHub.jsx:86, CaseStudyDetail.jsx:213, About.jsx:62)

action_items: Migrate/clean the one legacy post slug containing ':' and '’' (re-slug via _slug or delete)
Make PUT /api/admin/blog-autopilot return next_topic/next_run like GET so the admin status row stays populated after save
Fix fetchpriority -> fetchPriority in 4 JSX files and the <span> inside <option> hydration warning
critical_code_review_comments: generate_blog_post() has no post-validation on paragraph count/word count — a bad LLM response could insert a 2-paragraph 'post'. Consider validating len(body) >= 6 before insert.
server.py is 1425 lines; blog autopilot + LLM helpers should move to their own module.
_autopilot_generate_once dedupes on slug_hint only; if the LLM title-slug already exists it silently falls back to slug_hint + uuid — acceptable, but next_index advances even on duplicate topics.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_case_studies.py (fixed stale hardcoded BASE_URL fallback -> reads /app/frontend/.env; was causing 9 false 404 failures)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `pytest tests/ -k 'not test_run_generates_valid_post'` for fast regression; the excluded test makes a real Gemini call and creates a real blog post (delete it after). Public post fetch is wrapped: GET /api/blog/<slug> -> {post, related}. Autopilot generate-now took ~35-90s. Only known failure is the legacy dirty-slug post assertion in TestExistingSlugs/test_generated_posts_public_and_clean.
rca_of_the_issue: Dirty slug: _slug() strips punctuation correctly now, but the offending post was generated before the fix and stored in MongoDB; no migration was run, so GET /api/blog still lists the colon slug. Status-row blanking: PUT handler returns _get_autopilot() (raw settings) while the frontend replaces its whole autopilot state with the PUT response, which has no next_topic/next_run keys.
